sentences.text: This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is preferred feeling aggrieved by the award dated 08-03-2022 in MACC No. 399/2017 by 16th Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur for enhancement of Rs. 4 lacs compensation.
3. Facts in brief are that claim for permanent physical disability was filed on 08-02-2017 before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur.
An application under Section 166 (1) of Motor Vehicles Act, was registered as Motor Accident Claim Case No. 399/17 and the respondents contested the case.

4. The Tribunal framed issues and recorded the evidence and passed an award of Rs. 6,70,303/- and ordered to pay the compensation from the date of award and also given right of recovery to respondent No. 3 and 4 against the respondent Nos. 1and 2.
5.

This appeal has been preferred by the appellant that rate of interest is to be enhanced to 12 % per annum and to be ordered to pay compensation fully by the respondent Nos. 3 and 4.
6.

Facts in brief are that an application under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 was preferred for a compensation of Rs. 24,14,000/- regarding injuries caused by negligent driving of Vehicle No.
CG-04-JD-7950 by respondent No. 2, owned by respondent No. 1 and insured by respondent No. 3 and 4.
Regarding accident it was stated that on 15-06-2016 at about 1:00 PM, the respondent No. 2 dashed the appellant in front of Deepak Kirana Stores at Panagar District Jabalpur.
At the time of accident, the age of appellant was 39 years and he was running a general and grocery store at Panagar.
He earns a total of Rs. 12,000/- per month from that general and grocery store.
He was treated at Primary Health Centre, Panagar, Mohanlal Hargovindas Hospital and despite treatment he got 50% permanent physical disability.
7. The respondent Nos. 1 and 2 did not appear.
The respondent Nos. 3 and 4 contested the case.

He advanced his defence of contributory negligence of the claimant/appellant and also submitted that looking to the profession of appellant, the so-called permanent disability does not result into loss of income.

8. The Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of Sheikh Wahidurehman as (PW-1) Dr.
Sharad Dwivedi as (PW-2) and admitted the documents as Ex. P/1 and Ex. P/122.

The respondent Nos. 3 and 4 recorded the evidence of Administrative Officer Siddharth Bakke as DW-1 and put in evidence Ex. D/1 to Ex. D/6.
9.

Appreciating the evidence, the Tribunal found proved that the appellant/applicant sustained injury due to negligence of driving of Vehicle No. CG-04-JD-7950 by respondent No. 2, owned by respondent No. 1 and insured by respondent No. 3 and 4.

The Tribunal also found proved that the earning capacity of the appellant has been reduced to 20% due to physical disability caused to the appellant and also assessed the age of the appellant as 42 years and the income of the appellant as Rs. 10,000/- per month and entitled for a total claim of Rs. 6,70,303/- in the following heads :-
 (a) Loss of future earning Rs. 4,20,

10. The Tribunal also recorded the finding in paragraph-17 of the award that on the date of accident,
the respondent No. 2 does not possess the valid and effective driving licence to drive the Vehicle No.
CG-04-JD-7950 and there was breach of conditions of the policy.
So, ordered to pay the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 with right to recover the amount from the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and also to pay interest @ 7% per annum from the date of award.
11. This appeal has been preferred feeling aggrieved by the award dated 08-03-2022 on the ground that the tribunal ought to have passed the award treating the loss of income as 50%.
The Tribunal ought to have taken into consideration the situation of Covid-19 lockdown in delay of proceedings and ought to have awarded interest from the date of application.
The tribunal ought to have compensated treating the income of the appellant as Rs. 15,000/- per month.
Rate of interest ought to have awarded as 12 % per annum.
Non- pecuniary heads ought to have been awarded adequately.

12. Heard.
13.
Counsel for the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 opposed the prayer.

14. Perused the record.
15.

On perusal of the testimony of Dr. Sharad Dwivedi (PW-2) and the part of the body of the injured in the accident i.e. elbow of right hand of the appellant, the finding of the Tribunal regarding loss of 20% income due to injuries, does not call for interference.
16. Assessment of income is also proper.

Non-pecuniary heads have been adequately compensated,
they does not require interference.
The only question to be examined is as to whether Tribunal was justified in awarding the interest from the date of award instead of date of application.

sentences.text: The tribunal has recorded the finding in paragraph-37 that a claim application was filed on 08-02-2017 and respondent Nos. 3 to 4 filed written statement on 04-10-2017, issues were framed on 27-10-2017 and the case was fixed for evidence on 04-01-2018 and thereafter, the appellant prolonged the proceedings.
Perusal of proceedings discloses that dring this period, the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 has consumed time from 04-03-2021 to 25-02-2022.
Thus, a whole year period was consumed by the respondent Nos. 3 and 4.

Delay cannot be blamed to applicant about a period of 1 year i.e. 15-03-2022 to 04-03-2021 also due to the period of lockdown for Covid-19.
18.
Rest of the period is not such that appellant be deprived from interest.
I have considered that fact that who are responsible to cause injuries did not came forward to help the victim.
So, the order of Tribunal denying the interest from the date of filing of application is not justified from the proceedings of the record.

19. Hence, this appeal is allowed and paragraph-38.1 is modified that the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 shall pay the interest from the date of application i.e.06-02-2017 till realisation at the rate of 7% per annum.
The respondent Nos. 3 and 4 have a right to recover the same from the respondent Nos. 1 and 2.
(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE PG Sheikh Wahidurehman Siddique vs Prithviraj Singh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42226589/
